units.behavior: Every pull request prints its boundary delta, and the job cannot block a merge. A new pr-checks.yml job (the workflow runs on pull_request, :3-7) runs npm run qc:boundaries and prints the per-piece delta against the committed baseline. It is not in the Lint and Test aggregator's needs list (pr-checks.yml:700-721) and its gate step exits 0 unconditionally on the gate's own command line: the step's run is npm run qc:boundaries || true, so the step succeeds whatever the gate returns; the one other accepted form is an explicit set +e line before the command followed by a final exit 0. A bare trailing exit 0 line is not accepted: GitHub Actions runs a run step under bash -e on ubuntu-latest (bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail when shell: bash is set, as several pr-checks.yml steps do, e.g. :474), so a failing qc:boundaries line ends the step with exit 1 before a trailing exit 0 runs. continue-on-error is not used, because it lets the step exit 1 and only keeps the job from failing. The aggregator fails when any needed job's result is not success, skipped included (:725-736; analysis correction 28), so a report-only job inside it would block merges. Branch protection is unchanged. Until U66 is main-verified this job cannot fail on a grown baseline, so the parent checks each PR's baseline delta at review in that window, and any growth needs the owner's head-bound OWNER-RULING under sub-decision 8 (the decision's ledgerPlacement.reviewClasses). Red-first: a scripts/__tests__ jest pin parses pr-checks.yml (the yaml devDependency) and asserts that the job exists, is absent from lint-and-test.needs, and has a gate step whose qc:boundaries command is itself unconditional ('npm run qc:boundaries || true' on that line, or a set +e line before it and a final exit 0 line), with no continue-on-error on the step or the job; the pin's checker rejects a fixture step whose only guard is a bare trailing exit 0; red today (no job). units.behavior: The boundary gate blocks regressions. The gate exits 1 on any violation or runtime cycle not in the committed baseline, and on a baseline that gains an entry relative to the PR's merge base; a baseline entry whose violation is gone must be removed in the same PR (the baseline never carries a fixed edge). The pr-checks job joins the Lint and Test aggregator's needs (pr-checks.yml:700-721) and is never skipped (docs-only PRs take a no-op step, as prepare-build does). Its gate step drops U64's '|| true' (and any set +e or trailing exit 0), so the gate's exit code is the step's and a gate exit 1 fails the job; U64's exit-0 workflow pin is inverted in this unit. Baseline growth follows owner sub-decision 8: a PR that grows the baseline carries the owner's head-bound OWNER-RULING (a comment beginning OWNER-RULING <40-hex head> and the owner-ruled label); the job accepts growth only when both are on the PR for its current head and the ruling comment's author login equals the owner's login, pinned in the gate's config as SwiggitySwerve (the repository owner, and the author of all 14 packet rulings units.json records on f50e76fe4), and otherwise fails naming the decision. validate-roadmap.mjs:533-535 checks the label and the comment but no author; the job does not copy that gap. The login check refuses a ruling from any other account; it cannot tell the owner from an agent using the owner's gh credentials (the parent posts rulings the owner gives in chat under that account, with a disclosure), so that distinction stays with the parent's review, not the job. How the job sees a ruling posted after the push: the ruling can only be posted once the head exists, so the job's first run on a growing head fails. The job reads the PR's labels and comments live with gh when it runs (as validate-roadmap.mjs --github reads them; the job declares permissions contents: read and pull-requests: read), never from github.event.pull_request, whose labels are frozen at the triggering event and are replayed unchanged on a re-run. After the owner posts the comment and the label, the parent runs gh run rerun <run id> --failed, which re-runs the failed boundary job and the Lint and Test aggregator that failed with it; the re-run reads the ruling and passes. pull_request types stay [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review] (pr-checks.yml:7): adding 'labeled' would re-run every job of the workflow on each label event, and skipping the other jobs on those runs would fail the aggregator, which counts skipped as not success (:725-736).
